title: Natty Dominique, Kid Ory's band in San Francisco, and Ory's leadership
summary: He recalls Natty Dominique sitting in at Chicago's Beehive, then joining Kid Ory in 1953 at the Hangover Club in San Francisco and describes Ory's leadership and the band's players.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I think that was only for a couple of months. Remember once Dr. Bichet, his brother, Sidney's brother, the trombonist, came up. Were you there when he sat in one night? No, I wasn't. Might have been a different engagement or something. I think I even have a photograph. I don't remember if you were in that photo. I don't believe you were. I don't think. Did you ever play with Natty Dominic? Well, he sat in the Beehive. It's a club on the south side of Chicago. I was playing there with Miff Mole and Darnell Howard and Booker T. Washington. He came in a couple of times. Afternoon sessions, I thought. Sunday afternoon. Played, but I was scheduled to make an album with him on trumpet. But it didn't pan out. And there was late years. License trouble or something. Yeah, right before I left Chicago a year or so, before we made a date with Natty. And we were hoping to have you. Oh, yeah. I think Birch Smith. Yeah, and Birch, of course. But at the time we got those arranged, but you were out of town. And we used, Birch used Lil Armstrong. And I used Turvalon. Oh, you might tell a little bit about Ori. You may not even get it out loud here. Oh, well, it was very enjoyable playing with his band. I was with him over a year out in San Francisco. Had he ever heard you before? How did he happen to... I don't think he'd ever heard even... Well, maybe a couple of records. Al Hanson, here he comes again. He got me a job in Ori's band through extensive correspondence. And he got me to come out to the coast and join Ori. Anything about Ori's leadership? Anything... See, Mutt was out of the band at that time, wasn't he? Yes, he was. Did you ever play Mutt at all? No. I guess Mutt was dead in 1948. Yes, I was sorry to hear that. You didn't join Ori until around 52 or something like that, wasn't he? 53. 53. 53. August, I think, or September, 53. Had four weeks at the Hangover Club. Then we went to Los Angeles, and the idea was to play down there at the Beverly Caverns. That job didn't pan out. And we came back to the Hangover for a full year's contract. Yeah. And that's... During that time, I sort of fell in love with the city, and I actually call that my home now. Anything in particular about Ori and his leadership? Oh, he was very much the leader. He dominated the scene very much. Very fine leader, too. Did he have rehearsals much in your engagement ever? No. Things you looked out on the stand? No, we rehearsed for recording days, I saw. Yep. Let's see. Well, yeah, we had a rehearsal before we started the year's contract, but not before the four weeks. So, just how... Most things just worked out by head, or did he ever use any arrangements? Oh, all by head. Anything about the other players of the band from New Orleans, like... Oh, yeah, Ed Garland. Yes. Oh, I had a lot of enjoyment playing with that section. Ram Hall. Yeah.
